items.title: How does nav shape change time-to-find?
items.description: Every level of a menu costs the visitor two things: scanning the choices on that screen (which grows slowly as choices are added, since people scan in chunks, not one at a time) and clicking through to the next screen (a fixed cost per level, regardless of how many choices were on it). Drag 'choices per level' to see scanning cost grow, or 'levels deep' to see the fixed per-click cost multiply. At Trailhead's redesigned depth of 3 with about 4 choices per level, this reproduces roughly the few seconds a visitor actually spends finding the rain jacket.
items.compute: const scanTime = 0.35 * Math.log2(params.breadthPerLevel + 1); const perLevelTime = scanTime + 0.5; return { findTime: params.depth * perLevelTime };

outputs.label: Estimated time to find the item
